 3 days ago Liverpool legend Mohamed Salah became Egypt’s all-time record goalscorer on Friday night.
 By Chris Shaw
 Previous Next The forward, whose glittering and historic nine-year Reds career concluded in the past summer, struck twice for his country in a 5-0 win against Malawi in Africa Cup of Nations qualifying.
 That double increased Salah’s tally for the men’s national team to 70, overtaking the previous leader Hossam Hassan.
 Now at Trabzonspor, Salah departed Liverpool having ripped up the record books at club level too.
 Between 2017 and 2026 at Anfield, he scored 257 goals in 442 appearances and lifted eight major honours – including two Premier League titles and the Champions League.
